scope: Source-free provenance for the linux/amd64 v1 native tool pins beside the existing linux/arm64 pins. No provider registration, corpus run, target execution, release or scale claim.

builder.linux: official go1.25.0 linux/arm64 SDK inside image sha256:7b140f374b289a7c2befc338f42ebe6441b7ea838a042bbd5acbfca6ec875818 (debian:bookworm-slim, the T45.1b worker image), --network none, GOPROXY=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local
builder.cross_check: go1.25.0 darwin/arm64 toolchain; amd64 outputs byte-identical to the Linux builder

tools.recipe: go1.25.0 GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0 GOARM64=v8.0|GOAMD64=v1 go build -mod=readonly -buildvcs=false -trimpath -ldflags=-X=main.rulesGoRepositoryName=@rules_go
go1.25.0 GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0 GOARM64=v8.0|GOAMD64=v1 go build -mod=readonly -buildvcs=false -trimpath ./cmd/scip-go
tools.qualification: The retained T45.1b arm64 image is not byte-reproduced: its recorded BuildInfo (go1.25.0, (devel), -trimpath, CGO_ENABLED=0, GOARM64=v8.0) and nine dependencies equal the recipe output, which is 110 bytes smaller. go install @v0.2.7, workspace mode, darwin and Linux hosts and upstream's go1.25.7 release binary were also ruled out. The arm64 pin stays the historical image; the amd64 pin is the deterministic recipe output from the same source graph.

unchanged_arm64_only: Bazel C sysroot tools/cc-sysroot.zip (compilerDigest) and its aarch64-linux-gnu paths: an amd64 sysroot must be sealed on an x86_64 host before Bazel can run there
